rounds.observation: None of the 20 evaluated designs is feasible: 11 returned no geometry and the 9 that ran each violate at least one constraint. The constraint limits back-computed from the margins are max_g <= 12, bondline temperature <= 450 K and bluntness <= 1.2. The heatshield mass limit is not stated. Geometry failures come from a small cone angle combined with high bluntness or large diameter. A rough fit to the reported negative cone lengths gives a validity condition of about 0.917*b*cos(theta) + 0.133*(1-cos(theta)) < 0.5, checked by hand against the data. I keep it below about 0.46. The mass-fraction ratio scales roughly with D^2 and falls with cone angle, about 0.087*D^2 relative to the limit at 70 deg. A diameter of about 3.0-3.3 m with high cone angle should therefore sit near the mass limit. Peak g is set mainly by |gamma|: about 11.4 at 3.08 deg, 11.9 at 3.5 deg and 12.7 at 3.96 deg, so |gamma| must stay at or below roughly 3.5 deg. Peak heat flux fits q ~ 295e3*sqrt((m/A)*sin|gamma|/(b*D)) to within about 5-10%, and bondline temperature rise fits roughly 14*Y^0.4*sin|gamma|^-0.3 with Y = sqrt((m/A)/(b*D*sin|gamma|)). Both fits are my own regressions on 9 points. So the region to target is D about 2.7-3.3 m, b about 1.0-1.18, theta 66-70 deg and |gamma| about 2-3.6 deg.
evidence: C-1b6a532a4589: margin_g 0.00983 at 11.882 g gives limit 12; T 456.89 at margin -0.01531 gives limit 450; C-763297ba691c: b 1.2307 at margin -0.02558 gives limit 1.2.

Invalid geometries: C-ef541f66418a (b 1.18, theta 61.9), C-68844c149dc6 (b 0.99, theta 59.7, D 2.0) and C-8918773e968b (b 0.87, theta 52.7, D 4.05). Valid: C-763297ba691c (b 1.23, theta 69.8), C-7929904365f5 and C-0f5c4bbcbbf2. High bluntness needs theta near 70 deg.

Mass fraction: C-763297ba691c (D 2.5, margin +0.45), C-7929904365f5 (D 3.63, -0.18), C-d0ebb2a4a17d (D 4.3, -0.69), C-a7c3287a38ba (D 4.36, -0.99). Low-theta rows C-04af890b3186 (theta 31, -0.52) and C-697f9dd9337a (theta 38, +0.08) show higher mass per D^2.
g vs gamma: C-d0ebb2a4a17d gamma -3.08 gives 11.45 g, C-1b6a532a4589 gamma -3.50 gives 11.88 g, C-7929904365f5 gamma -3.96 gives 12.71 g, C-951f544259a7 gamma -5.09 gives 14.58 g.
Heat flux scaling holds across rows: C-763297ba691c 447k, C-d0ebb2a4a17d 333k, C-7929904365f5 320k, C-697f9dd9337a 668k, C-1b6a532a4589 1.07M. The fitted constant is 280-308k.
Bondline T rises as gamma gets shallower and diameter smaller: C-1b6a532a4589 (D 1.65) 457 K, C-d0ebb2a4a17d 404 K, C-0f5c4bbcbbf2 (steep, D 3.86) 367 K.
rounds.mechanism: Ballistic-entry scaling from prior knowledge, checked against the rows above. Peak stagnation heat flux scales with sqrt(ballistic coefficient * sin gamma / nose radius). Bondline temperature follows the integrated heat load, which grows with a low-drag, small-nose-radius, shallow-entry pulse. A larger diameter lowers the ballistic coefficient and so lowers both objectives, but it is capped by heatshield mass fraction. A larger bluntness raises the nose radius and lowers heat flux, but it is capped at 1.2 and by geometry validity, which needs a large cone half-angle. Steeper entry lowers bondline temperature but raises g, which is capped at 12. Because the reference is 450 K over a 150 K range, bondline temperature dominates the hypervolume. The best feasible region should therefore be the corner of maximum diameter, maximum bluntness, theta about 70 deg and |gamma| near the g limit.
rounds.uncertainty: The geometry-validity fit, mass-fraction scaling and g(gamma) relation are inferred from 9 valid points and can be off by a few percent. Diameters of 3.3-3.4 m sit at the mass boundary, and |gamma| of 3.5-3.6 deg sits at the g boundary. Whether high bluntness and cone angle lower g at a given gamma is unknown. The bondline-temperature fit has about 5-10 K scatter. Low-gamma probes (2-2.4 deg) risk unmodelled skip-out or long-pulse effects.

rounds.observation: Of 40 evaluations, 19 are feasible and 3 sit on the front, all at cone_half_angle 70 (the maximum), bluntness 1.18 and diameter 3.2-3.3. The constraint limits implied by the margins are max_g <= 12, bondline temperature <= 450 K and bluntness <= 1.2. The heatshield mass fraction margin depends only on diameter, bluntness and cone angle. It falls from 0.106 at D=3.2 to 0.049 at D=3.3 and is -0.009 at D=3.4, so it reaches zero near D=3.38. g depends only on diameter and flight-path angle. Because the hypervolume reference is 450 K, temperature carries far more weight than heat flux: 1 K of temperature is worth about 0.0067 of normalised HV, while 10 kW/m2 is worth about 0.004 x (450-T)/150. The best strategy is to sit at the largest buildable diameter, maximum bluntness and maximum cone angle, and sweep flight-path angle from the g limit (about -3.6) to shallow angles to cover the front. All numbers below are my own extrapolations from the tabulated rows.
evidence: C-0149edccdafc (D3.3, gamma -2.8) and C-acebb6e3a142 (D3.3, gamma -3.3) show that steeper entry lowers bondline temperature (396.4 to 391.1 K) and raises heat flux (235.7k to 246.6k).

C-8e40abb65d5d (D3.4) has margin -0.009 on mass fraction, while C-acebb6e3a142 (D3.3) has +0.049 and C-b35840b70e3f (D3.2) has +0.106. The mass limit is therefore near D~3.38 and I stay at or below 3.375.

The D=3.0, b=1.18 gamma sweep (C-8ea797b7e7be, C-665a0318f7e1, C-71a80f5821da, C-1d43ab7c8761, C-6235648fc97f, C-c4e456e7ba92) gives T = 413.4, 407.7, 402.5, 400.2, 395.8, 393.8 K and g = 9.62 to 11.85. This gives about 1.6 g/deg near -3.6, so g=12 is reached near -3.69 at D=3.0.
g rises about 0.037 per 0.1 m of diameter (C-8e40abb65d5d 11.681 at D3.4 vs 11.527 at D3.0, same -3.4). At D~3.36 I therefore cap gamma at about -3.57 to keep g < 12.
Heat flux scales roughly as D^-1.5 (C-6235648fc97f 285.7k vs C-8e40abb65d5d 238.3k at gamma -3.4) and falls with higher bluntness (C-c26631ea4756 with b=1.0 is worse than the b=1.18 trend).

Lower cone angle and lower bluntness raise both objectives and reduce the mass margin (C-6aa6f3f26271, C-d9f3953251f5, C-189429d88e59), so cone stays at 70. Bluntness limit is 1.2 (margin 0.01667 at 1.18).
Geometry failures (C-12a940ca6a66 etc.) all involve small cone angles. Cone 70 and D>=3 has never failed, so I avoid that region.
rounds.mechanism: Ballistic-entry scaling: a larger diameter lowers the ballistic coefficient and, through a larger nose radius, lowers stagnation heat flux (~D^-1.5) and integrated heat load. A steeper entry shortens the heating pulse, which lowers bondline temperature but raises peak flux and g. Higher bluntness enlarges the nose radius and lowers both objectives. The feasible optimum therefore sits on the intersection of the mass-fraction limit (D~3.36-3.375), the bluntness limit (~1.2), the maximum cone angle (70) and the g limit (gamma ~ -3.55 to -3.58). Sweeping gamma at fixed D~3.36 traces the front from about 387 K / 243k W/m2 down to about 412 K / 203k W/m2.
rounds.uncertainty: The mass-fraction margin near D=3.36-3.375 is extrapolated (predicted +0.003 to +0.015), so the D>=3.37 points may violate it. g near -3.57 to -3.58 has predicted margins of only 0.3-0.6%. Bluntness 1.2 sits exactly on its limit (margin 0), so I use 1.195 for most designs. Shallow-gamma behaviour (-1.6) is extrapolated beyond the tabulated range, and my predicted temperatures could be off by 1-3 K.
